title: Why Losing $1,000 Hurts Twice as Much as Gaining $1,000
alt_title_1: Kahneman & Tversky's 2x Loss Trap Draining Your Portfolio
alt_title_2: Prospect Theory Explained: Stop Panic-Selling Market Dips
description_hook: In their landmark 1979 Econometrica paper on Prospect Theory, Daniel Kahneman and Amos Tversky showed that financial losses hurt roughly twice as much psychologically as equivalent gains feel good. Here is how to stop loss aversion from sabotaging long-term compounding.

scenes.headline: Why Losing $1,000 Stings Twice as Hard
scenes.stat_label: PSYCHOLOGICAL RATIO OF LOSS PAIN TO EQUAL GAIN
bullets: Gain $1,000 -> brief relief half as intense
scenes.narration: Losing one thousand dollars hurts roughly twice as much psychologically as winning the exact same thousand dollars feels good, and it warps your wealth.
scenes.source: Kahneman & Tversky, 'Prospect Theory', Econometrica (1979); Tversky & Kahneman (1992)

scenes.headline: Kahneman & Tversky's 1979 Breakthrough
bullets: Classic economics assumed symmetric rational choices
Real humans weigh losses ~2x heavier than equal gains
scenes.narration: In their landmark 1979 Econometrica paper on Prospect Theory, psychologists Daniel Kahneman and Amos Tversky proved human value perception is asymmetric: the mental sting of a loss dwarfs an equal gain.
scenes.source: Kahneman & Tversky, 'Prospect Theory: An Analysis of Decision under Risk', Econometrica (1979)

scenes.headline: Daily Portfolio Checks Trigger Threat Alarms
scenes.left_body: Sees noisy red days -> panic-sells dips or hoards idle cash
scenes.right_body: Ignores daily noise -> captures decades of equity growth
scenes.narration: That wiring turns daily stock-checking into self-sabotage. Watching normal market dips triggers evolutionary threat alarms, pushing investors to panic-sell lows or hoard idle cash for years.

scenes.headline: Widen Your Evaluation Window
scenes.stat_subtext: Fewer portfolio peeks -> far less emotional drag
scenes.narration: Neutralize loss aversion by widening your evaluation window: automate monthly index contributions and inspect your portfolio once per quarter instead of five times before lunch.

scenes.headline: Remove the Live Ticker From Your Pocket
bullets: Delete live brokerage widgets from your phone home screen
Review allocations on one calm date each quarter
scenes.narration: Delete live brokerage widgets from your phone today so temporary market noise stops hijacking thirty-year compounding decisions.
scenes.source: Mind & Margin rule of thumb inspired by Kahneman & Tversky (1979) and Benartzi & Thaler (1995)
